title: Agent tracing records the raw prompt, tool arguments and tool output, and redaction is an opt-in hook
problem: I added tracing so I could debug my agent, and in doing so I built a second, permanent copy of every customer secret and every piece of personal data that ever passed through a prompt, in a system with different access control from the one the data came from.
symptom: A trace viewer shows a full system prompt with an API key in it, or a tool result containing a customer record, and the same payload is now in a third-party SaaS backend, a log index and whatever else the OpenTelemetry pipeline fans out to.
why_now: Observability is the first thing an agent team adds and the redaction hook is the last: every major tracing SDK ships full-payload capture ON and a masking callback OFF, so the instrumented path is the leaking path and nothing in the SDK fails when the hook is absent.
existing: Masking and scrubbing callbacks exist in the tracing SDKs, but they are constructor arguments the integrator must supply; omitting one is silent and looks identical to a correctly configured client.
Provider-side zero-retention and log-redaction settings cover the model vendor's copy, not the copy the app's own tracing pipeline writes.
PII detectors such as Presidio can be wired into a masking hook, but nothing in the default install points them at the span attributes that carry the prompt.

build_hypothesis: A tracing wrapper that refuses to initialise without an explicit payload policy: the client takes a required argument that is either a redaction callable or the literal opt-out token, so the leaking configuration has to be typed out on purpose and is greppable in review.

check.manual_question: Name the code path that removes secrets and personal data from a span before it leaves this process. If tracing is enabled and no such path exists, what is in the trace of a request that carried a bearer token or a customer record?
check.rationale: A tracing SDK is initialised and no masking, redaction or scrubbing hook appears anywhere in the shipped code, which means spans carry whatever the prompt and the tool output contained. It can be wrong two ways: a collector-side processor or a gateway can strip payloads outside this repo, and a repo may capture only metadata by configuration rather than by a named hook, so a target with no signature and no mitigation is reported MANUAL rather than clean.
